subject: DPA redlines, subprocessor matrix, and eSign path (DocuSign vs Adobe) — timing
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@finpay.com>
To: alex_martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jared Miller <jared.miller@finpay.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA review and subprocessors — next steps

Alex —

Thanks for taking a look at FinPay’s standard DPA. I’m attaching our redlines — most of the commercial terms are already in our PO, but legal has flagged the subprocessor section and the data transfer wording. Procurement is also asking that signature happen via DocuSign so we can tie the signature to our PO system.

Key asks from FinPay legal/procurement:
- Confirmation of Redwood’s current subprocessor list and an exported CSV of the matrix (attached would be ideal).
- Clarify the notification window for new subprocessors and the objection process (we typically require a 30 calendar day objection window).
- Confirmation that we can execute the DPA via DocuSign; Adobe Sign is acceptable but DocuSign is preferred by our systems team.

Can you confirm turnaround? Our SOW kickoff is targeted for the week of Apr 25 so we need the DPA in signed form before then.

Thanks —
Elena
Procurement Manager, FinPay Inc.
Attachments: FinPay_DPA_Redlines_v1.pdf

From: alex_martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@finpay.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA review and subprocessors — next steps

Hi Elena — thanks for the redline and the clear timeline.

High-level response:
- We can provide the current subprocessor matrix as a CSV (I’ve attached our Q2 export and a proposed redline of our DPA).
- Redwood prefers to use a notification + objection model for new subprocessors. Given your timeline, we propose the following compromise to move quickly: a 21 calendar day objection window (instead of 30), with a 10-business-day expedited objection path for certain high-risk processors where both teams agree faster review is needed.
- DocuSign is fine for us — we can accept a single-envelope flow with two signers (Redwood contracts and Redwood finance) or a prioritized single-signer path if you need faster signature.

I’ve attached: redwood_dpa_proposal_v2.pdf (redlines called out) and subprocessor_matrix_q2_2027.csv. Laura and Rishi are looped in on legal/privacy questions below.

Could you confirm whether procurement must attach the PO to the DPA envelope and who will be the initial signer on your side? If we can get the envelope to contracts@redwood.com by Apr 18 we should be able to execute by Apr 21 and still hit your kickoff.

—Alex
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_dpa_proposal_v2.pdf, subprocessor_matrix_q2_2027.csv

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: alex_martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@finpay.com>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA review and subprocessors — next steps

Alex / Elena — quick legal notes from our side after an initial pass of FinPay’s redlines:

1) Objection window:
- We do not object to a defined window, but 30 calendar days is operationally heavy and will slow onboarding. Propose 21 calendar days for standard processors; carve out an emergency exception allowing us to onboard critical patches/providers with immediate notification (we’ll log and explain reasons).

2) Burden of proof:
- FinPay’s suggested requirement that Redwood "prove" specific mitigations before onboarding is workable only in limited cases. We prefer a clear objection scope (e.g., processors that handle unredacted PII or cryptographic key material). Otherwise we need a reasonable notice period and remediation commitments.

3) Execution path:
- DocuSign is acceptable. We prefer a single envelope that includes the redlined DPA and a reference to the PO. If FinPay requires embedded metadata (PO number, procurement code), include it in the envelope so our finance team can reconcile automatically.

4) Evidence and audits:
- FinPay asked for SOC2 reports and attestations — we can provide our current SOC2 Type II + pen test summary; for vendor-specific evidence we’ll provide point-in-time evidence for critical processors on request.

I’m attaching a short legal clean-up redline that narrows the objection triggers and includes the emergency exception language.

—Laura
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_dpa_legaledits_v1.pdf

From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@finpay.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, alex_martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jared Miller <jared.miller@finpay.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA review and subprocessors — next steps

Laura / Alex — thanks for the quick legal review and for proposing the 21 day compromise. Two quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Procurement systems: DocuSign is preferred because our PO system picks up the envelope ID and attaches it to the SOW automatically. If you can add PO# FINPAY-PO-4521 into the envelope metadata we’ll be able to route without manual steps.

2) Objection scope: we can accept the emergency exception but FinPay needs an explicit definition of high-risk processors (examples: persistent storage of unhashed SSNs, KMS providers storing customer keys, or processors with access to raw transaction payloads). If you can enumerate categories in the DPA we’ll expedite review for anything outside those categories.

I’ve uploaded our PO template as a stub (FinPay_PO_template.pdf) and marked the preferred signer on our side as contracts@finpay.com. If Redwood is okay with 21 day window + emergency onboarding carve-out and agrees to include processor categories as described, procurement will prepare the DocuSign envelope tonight.

—Elena

From: alex_martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@finpay.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA review and subprocessors — next steps

Elena — that works for us. Confirming the follow-ups and logistics: 

- Redwood accepts DocuSign as primary execution path. Please include PO# FINPAY-PO-4521 in envelope metadata and send to contracts@redwood.com; cc alex.martinez@redwood.ai.
- We accept a 21 calendar day general objection window. For the emergency onboarding carve-out, Redwood will provide written notice within 48 hours of onboarding and a post-facto rationale.
- We will add an enumeration of "high-risk processor" categories to Section 3.2 (examples per your note: storage of unredacted SSNs, KMS/key custody providers, processors that decrypt transaction payloads). The intent is to expedite review, not to expand procurement-level demands.
- Evidence: Redwood will attach SOC2 Type II and our latest pen test summary to the envelope. For processor-specific attestations we’ll provide point-in-time docs on request (we’ve attached our public matrix for reference).

Proposed timeline:
- Apr 18: FinPay sends DocuSign envelope to contracts@redwood.com (include PO and evidence).
- Apr 19–20: Redwood review and sign (if no substantive changes required).
- Apr 21: Target executed DPA in place.

If that timeline looks feasible I’m good to proceed. Priyom, can you confirm open billing/PO acceptance once the envelope is signed? Rishi, please confirm privacy language changes are acceptable and I’ll ask you to OK the final version once the envelope is received.

Thanks —
Alex
